subject: Reranker sensitivity, grounding metrics and probe requests — next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@talariahealth.com>, aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Reranker sensitivity, grounding metrics and probe requests — next steps

Lina / team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation and helpful context on the kinds of hallucination-y edge cases you see when clinicians push the assistant beyond its SOP scope. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can qualify model fit and give you a concrete pilot plan: 

1) High-level ask from Talaria: establish a RAG baseline that balances factual grounding with clinical answer quality. Key concerns: hallucinated recommendations, citations that point to wrong doc sections, and sensitivity of answer ranking when passages are semantically close.

2) Recommended model families for initial probes (we'll provide quantized variants to control cost):
   - Llama2-13B (instruction-tuned, q4f) — best cost/latency tradeoff for interactive throughput
   - Mistral-7B-instruct (higher instruction fidelity on concise clinical prompts)
   - Optionally: a small local cross-encoder reranker (cross-encoder-miniLM) for hard ranking points

3) RAG / retrieval settings we suggest to test first (we'll run these as controlled experiments):
   - Retriever k=8, chunk size 400–600 chars (overlapping 20%)
   - Embedding model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (or your existing vector factory if you'd prefer)
   - Reranker: cross-encoder re-rank stage vs. bi-encoder cosine-only baseline (we'll compare both)

4) Grounding metrics & pass/fail criteria we propose to capture quality/regression:
   - Precision@1 of grounded answers (does top answer cite correct document and section?)
   - Grounding recall across top-5 (are any gold passages present in top 5?)
   - Hallucination rate on a curated probe set (binary label: contains fabricated facts)
   - Clinician-rated utility (1–5) on sampled responses

5) Data we need from Talaria for qualification (small initial sample):
   - 40–60 representative queries (mix of high/low confidence) — we can augment with negative/ambiguous queries
   - Example gold passages (where available) or docIDs to validate grounding
   - Any internal logs of recent assistant failures (optional)

Attachments: I attached a starter probe set (talaria_probe_set_v1.csv) and an internal reranker benchmark we can run and share results from (reranker-bench-20261120.csv).

Next steps I propose:
 - You share the 40–60 query sample + any gold passage references (we can redact PHI if needed)
 - We run an initial A/B: bi-encoder retrieval vs. cross-encoder rerank on the two model families above, return a short evaluation with our metrics within 5 business days of receiving the sample
 - Quick follow-up call to review results and align on a 3-week pilot scope (we'll size infra and provide cost estimates)

If this sounds good I'll loop in our infra lead (Aditya) to stitch the evaluation harness to your dev/test vector store.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

--
Attachments: talaria_probe_set_v1.csv (CSV, 60 rows), reranker-bench-20261120.csv (CSV, summary metrics)

Thanks, Kimberly — this is exactly the kind of structure we wanted. A few quick clarifications before we share the sample set:

- On retrieval k: when you say k=8, is that ’k returned by the vector DB’ or the number of chunks you include in the LT prompt? Our current pipeline returns top-10 vectors but post-filters by recency; happy to have you override on your side.
- For the bi-encoder baseline, will you re-embed our docs or use our existing embeddings? We want apples-to-apples comparisons if possible.

We can get you 50 queries by EOD Monday. I'll also pull two tickets that show recent hallucinations so you can see concrete examples.

Small ask on security: procurement asked if Redwood will need any service account to access the QA vector store for the initial run — we prefer not to share production credentials. Can Aditya propose a read-only ingress approach or a sample export mechanism?

Appreciate it — Lina

Subject: Re: Reranker sensitivity, grounding metrics and probe requests — next steps

Lina — quick technical notes to address your questions and lay out what we'll run:

1) k semantics: we'll control k at the retrieval stage (what we ask the vector DB to return). For the experiment we recommend asking your DB for top-12 then deduplicate and re-chunk to yield an effective k=8 candidates to the generator/reranker. That gives headroom for recency and duplicates.

2) Embeddings: best for apples-to-apples is that we re-embed the probe documents with the same embedding model we use for evaluation. If you'd rather provide a static export of your current vector index (read-only export) we can run against that, but differences in embedding models can change recall and make comparisons noisy. We can support both in parallel.

3) Reranker options we will evaluate (implementations we'll test):
   - Bi-encoder (approx nearest neighbor) + generator-only re-rank (fastest, lowest cost)
   - Bi-encoder + small cross-encoder re-rank (cross-encoder-miniLM) — medium cost, often biggest uplift when passages are semantically similar
   - Heavy cross-encoder (cross-encoder-large) — best rank quality but ~3–5x latency and cost; good as a canary for high-risk queries

4) Probe instrumentation: we'll surface Precision@1, Grounded-Precision@1 (top answer cites a correct doc/section), Grounding Recall@5, hallucination flag rate, and a small clinician rubric (utility/accuracy). The reranker-bench-20261120.csv includes a sample run from a previous customer with the same metric set — use that as a template.

5) Security & access: we can operate via either
   - Your read-only export of the QA index (preferred, no account sharing), or
   - Temporary, scoped service account with read-only vector query access (we can provide a short-lived token and explicit IP allowlist).

If you send the 50 queries and either a zipped export or confirm the export path, we'll get the baseline A/B run started Monday and aim to return results within 5 business days.

Cheers,
Aditya
